data.title: Think harder about sociality and memory systems
data.contentMarkdown:
# Think harder about sociality and memory systems

*   thickening loose ties
*   creating opportunities for repeated, lightweight contact
*   making review activities feel integrated into a broader conversation somehow

Returning to this on [[2020-05-26]], these are still my top themes. The obvious temptation would be to go for some kind of social signaling, etc, but that’s just so boring…

[[Kanjun Qiu]] mentions some research (haven’t dug it up) that intimate connections require a combination of:

*   unplanned interactions
*   shared intense experiences
*   vulnerability / safety

[[2022-09-15]]: [[Taylor Rogalski]] shares a Will Wright game concept (<https://youtu.be/DJQpw0uR9AQ>) and asks:

> He’s sort of describing a social flash card game, where people recall and rank shared memories (like world events). Wonder how that maps to Orbit. Could there be a social game that uses the prompts you’ve collected?

backlinkedNotes.linkingNoteTitle: Memory system practice sessions are too disconnected from activities you actually care about
contextBlocks: Can we create something *like* a retrieval practice session, but much more strongly grounded in what you actually care about? More clearly connected with your actual goals? Situated in the actual activity or context? Embedded in a social context? [[zTLbubuUTz75EDoYizxCSXg:::Think harder about sociality and memory systems]]

backlinkedNotes.linkingNoteTitle: Current conception of Orbit is overly memory-focused; where’s the poetry?
contextBlocks: [[zTLbubuUTz75EDoYizxCSXg:::Think harder about sociality and memory systems]]

backlinkedNotes.linkingNoteTitle: Building a better memory system - Michael Nielsen
contextBlocks: Some very thoughtful comments from [[Michael Nielsen]] unpacking unusual directions for design research in memory systems. Particularly valuable are the background remarks, which emphasize meaning ([[z4ULp2KUgq3hBCJMWTUnLDX:::The dominant culture around spaced repetition memory systems is fixated on meaningless goals]]); depth of understanding, emotional connection ([[zPiRwRHQxGfF9Zej765PB8M:::The critical thing to optimize in spaced repetition memory systems is emotional connection to the review session and its contents]]), sociality ([[zTLbubuUTz75EDoYizxCSXg:::Think harder about sociality and memory systems]]).

backlinkedNotes.linkingNoteTitle: Liu, S., Abowitz, S., Liu, Y., Sterman, S., Almeda, S. G., & Kreminski, M. (2026). Creative Reading - Scaffolding Reading for Transformation
contextBlocks: They also briefly treat the issue of sociality, which seems very underexplored in these systems. (E.g. [[zTLbubuUTz75EDoYizxCSXg:::Think harder about sociality and memory systems]])

backlinkedNotes.linkingNoteTitle: Funnels, tubes, and fields, after Joe Edelman
contextBlocks: Joe’s description of fields highlights one key deficiency of my ideas around [[zPpaHZYKuBPyoDtgcsiZ9RV:::Programmable attention]]: {they’re still single-player-centric (see [[zTLbubuUTz75EDoYizxCSXg:::Think harder about sociality and memory systems]])}.
[[zTLbubuUTz75EDoYizxCSXg:::Think harder about sociality and memory systems]]
